bundles.name: Identity and Classification
bundles.description: Fixes what the product is, who is accountable for it, how it is typed, and which external coordinates denote it.
bundles.rationale: No downstream statement about composition, exposure or support can be joined or refuted until the product has a stable, non-date identifier and a declared namespace. SPDX makes every Element identifiable and attributable to an Agent; the SBOM minimum elements make supplier, name and unique identifier mandatory; purl and CPE supply the governed external coordinates.

layers.name: Product Identity
layers.description: The stable identity of the product as an offering, independent of any single release, package or deployment.

findings.name: Product Identity Record
findings.description: The authoritative record that fixes the product's master-system identifier, canonical name, issuing namespace, producer of record and the criterion separating it from adjacent offerings.

findings.name: Identifier Coordinates and Crosswalk
findings.description: Ecosystem-facing coordinates that let external systems match this product and its releases (Package URL, CPE, SWID, download location, content identifiers), plus the mapping and precedence between them.

findings.name: Family, edition, channel and SKU
findings.description: CoSWID software-meta separates product, product-family, edition, channel-type, colloquial-version and revision from the exact software-version. CSAF product trees use vendor/product/version branches, product groups and relationships among products. These group commercial variants (enterprise versus standard, OEM versus academic, LTS line) without treating each SKU as an unrelated product or collapsing them into a single version.

layers.name: Classification and Stewardship
layers.description: How the product is typed and what purpose it serves, and who is entitled to speak for each slice of its record.

findings.name: Software Classification and Purpose
findings.description: Controlled typing of the software (component type, primary and additional purpose, delivery model, regulatory class) that determines which downstream profiles and obligations apply.

findings.name: Producer Accountability and Record Stewardship
findings.description: The split of ownership and authority over the record: producer-side release facts versus operator-side deployment facts, who may publish binding statements, and what happens when stewardship lapses.

bundles.name: Release and Distribution
bundles.description: The published version lineage of the product and the channels, conditions and cryptographic evidence under which each release reaches a consumer.
bundles.rationale: A software product exists in the world as a series of dated, versioned, immutable publications. SBOM minimum elements require component version and a creation timestamp; SPDX and CycloneDX carry download location, hashes and signatures; RFC 3339 fixes how the times are written.

layers.name: Release Lineage
layers.description: Individual published releases, their version strings, states, publication events and the scheme that makes versions comparable.

findings.name: Release Record
findings.description: One published version of the product: its version string, publication event time and observation time, distribution channel, state and supersession links.

findings.name: Version Scheme and Ordering
findings.description: The declared versioning scheme and precedence rules that make version comparison, dependency ranges and affected-range statements decidable rather than guessed.

findings.name: Patch versus upgrade and tag types
findings.description: CoSWID and NISTIR 8060 define four tag types used at different lifecycle points: corpus (pre-install media), primary (installed component), patch (incremental fix that MUST NOT change software-version) and supplemental (site-added metadata). Patch tags MUST link with rel=patches to the patched software. Upgrade replaces primary tags and changes version metadata. This distinction is a frequent omission in product catalogues that only store version strings.

layers.name: Distribution and Integrity
layers.description: Where a release may legitimately be obtained, under what access conditions, and the cryptographic evidence that a fetched artifact is the released artifact.

findings.name: Distribution Channel and Availability
findings.description: Authoritative download locations and registries for a release, the access conditions attached to them, and how long prior releases stay retrievable.

findings.name: Artifact Integrity and Signature
findings.description: Hashes, signatures and signing identities that let a consumer verify a fetched artifact, together with the verification outcome and any reproducibility claim.

bundles.name: Composition and Supply Chain
bundles.description: What the release is made of as declared in a bill of materials, how declared dependencies were resolved, and what provenance and development-practice evidence stands behind the build.
bundles.rationale: SBOM minimum elements make component name, version, supplier, unique identifier and dependency relationships mandatory, with declared depth and known unknowns; SLSA defines what provenance must state; SSDF defines the practice claims that condition how much weight that evidence carries.

layers.name: Declared Composition
layers.description: The bill of materials as a governed document about a release, and the dependency constraints and resolutions it records.

findings.name: Bill of Materials Document
findings.description: The SBOM treated as a dated, authored document about one release: its format and specification version, author, creation time, declared depth and explicitly declared known unknowns.

findings.name: Dependency Graph and Resolution
findings.description: Declared dependency constraints with scope and optionality, the concrete releases that satisfied them at build time, and the pinning that makes the resolution reproducible.

findings.name: Coverage, completeness and known unknowns
findings.description: CISA 2026 replaces NTIA Depth with Coverage (horizontal and vertical breadth) and requires explicitly identifying unknown information. CycloneDX compositions aggregate completeness as complete, incomplete, incomplete first-party only, incomplete third-party only or unknown. SPDX Sbom may carry multiple sbomTypes. An SBOM that omits unknowns is less operable than one that marks them. Completeness is a quality measurement of the composition evidence, not of the software.

layers.name: Build Provenance and Development Assurance
layers.description: Verifiable statements about what built the release from which inputs, and about the producer's secure development practices.

findings.name: Build Provenance Attestation
findings.description: Machine-verifiable provenance identifying the build platform and builder, the top-level inputs and source revision, the parameters used, and the build-integrity level the provenance supports.

findings.name: Secure Development Practice Assurance
findings.description: Claims about the producer's secure development practices, the evidence for each claim, and whether the claim is self-attested, customer-audited or third-party assessed.

bundles.name: Rights and Licensing
bundles.description: The licence under which a release is offered, the obligations inherited from third-party components, and the restrictions on who may use, receive or re-export it.
bundles.rationale: SPDX separates declared from concluded licensing and carries copyright and attribution text; SBOM minimum elements now include licence at component level. Obligations and restrictions determine whether a lawful deployment is possible at all, which no other layer answers.

layers.name: Licence Identification
layers.description: What licence applies to a release, how it was determined, and who may change it.

findings.name: Licence Declaration and Expression
findings.description: The licence expression applying to a release, distinguishing what the producer declared from what an analyst concluded, with the copyright holder and any licence change across releases.

layers.name: Obligations and Restrictions
layers.description: What the product must ship or make available because of what it contains, and who may lawfully receive and use it.

findings.name: Third-Party Attribution Obligations
findings.description: Obligations inherited from bundled third-party components: attribution notices that must ship, reciprocal obligations and their reach, and corresponding-source availability duties with their duration.

findings.name: Use and Export Restrictions
findings.description: Restrictions on who may obtain, run or re-export the product, including entitlement requirements, field-of-use exclusions, jurisdictional controls and documented waivers.

bundles.name: Deployment and Operation
bundles.description: Where releases actually run: deployed instances, their hosting environments, the configuration in effect and the interfaces they expose or consume.
bundles.rationale: Software has a second life as an operated system, and exposure questions are unanswerable from producer-side records alone. CycloneDX recognises operations and decommission lifecycle phases and separates services from components; CSAF product trees and SBOM access-control practice both presuppose an operator-held inventory.

layers.name: Deployed System Inventory
layers.description: Concrete running installations and the environments that host them.

findings.name: Deployed Instance Record
findings.description: One running installation of a specific release: its operator-side identifier, the version observed running, the window over which it ran, its purpose and its criticality.

findings.name: Hosting Environment and Platform
findings.description: The environment class, platform stack, jurisdictional location and network exposure of the host on which instances run.

layers.name: Runtime Configuration and Interfaces
layers.description: What the deployed software is actually doing: effective configuration and drift, and the external services and data flows it touches.

findings.name: Effective Configuration State
findings.description: The configuration actually in effect on an instance, its deviation from the released default or hardened baseline, and the change events that produced it. This matters because exploitability assessments are frequently conditional on configuration.

findings.name: External Interfaces and Data Flows
findings.description: Services, endpoints and data flows a deployed instance exposes or consumes, including third-party services that are dependencies but never shipped as components.

bundles.name: Lifecycle, Support and Security Response
bundles.description: How long the product is maintained, how fixes are delivered, and how published vulnerabilities are mapped to versions, instances and exploitability judgements.
bundles.rationale: The Cyber Resilience Act obliges manufacturers to handle vulnerabilities across the lifecycle and to report actively exploited vulnerabilities; CSAF supplies the machine-readable advisory and VEX structure; ISO/IEC/IEEE 12207 frames maintenance and disposal. These are distinct decision surfaces from composition.

layers.name: Support Lifecycle
layers.description: Support status, end-of-life milestones and the mechanics by which fixes reach deployed instances.

findings.name: Support Status and End of Life
findings.description: The producer's binding statement about how long a product line or release receives fixes, the dated milestones that end that obligation, and what happens to instances that outlive it.

findings.name: Update and Patch Delivery
findings.description: How fixes reach deployed instances: channels, mechanism, default automation, separability of security fixes from feature change, and evidence that an update was actually applied.

layers.name: Vulnerability and Advisory
layers.description: Published notices affecting the product and the product-specific judgement of whether a contained vulnerability is actually exploitable.

findings.name: Advisory and Exposure Mapping
findings.description: Notices of defects or vulnerabilities and the mapping from each notice to affected version ranges, contained components and deployed instances, with severity and any authority-reporting duty.

findings.name: Exploitability Assessment
findings.description: The product-specific determination of whether a vulnerability present in a contained component is actually exploitable in this product or deployment, with a recognised justification and its conditions.

findings.name: Remediation, entitlements and restart
findings.description: CSAF remediations carry category, date, details, product or group ids, URL, restart-required and entitlements. Entitlements here are access gates on a remediation (who may obtain the fix), not the intellectual-property license of the software. CoSWID activation-status and entitlement-key similarly record install-time activation without storing unprotected license secrets. Restart-required is an operational constraint on deployed systems.

bundles.name: Quality, Conformance and Regulatory
bundles.description: What quality the product is specified and measured against, what verification evidence exists, and what regulatory documentation must be produced and retained to place it on a market.
bundles.rationale: ISO/IEC 25010 supplies a governed quality model for specification and evaluation; the Cyber Resilience Act attaches conformity assessment, CE marking and technical documentation duties to products with digital elements. Both are decision surfaces an agent must be able to interrogate and neither is covered by composition or operations layers.

layers.name: Quality and Verification
layers.description: Specified quality characteristics with their measures, and the evidence that a release was verified against them.

findings.name: Quality Characteristics and Measures
findings.description: The quality characteristics selected for this product from a governed quality model, the measure and target defined for each, and the values actually measured on a named release.

findings.name: Verification and Test Evidence
findings.description: Evidence that a release was verified: which activities were performed, how each result binds to the exact artifact digest tested, and which defects were knowingly accepted at release.

layers.name: Regulatory Conformity
layers.description: Which market regimes apply, which conformity route was taken, and what documentation must exist and be retained.

findings.name: Conformity Assessment and Technical Documentation
findings.description: The regulatory regimes in scope for placing the product on each target market, the conformity assessment route used, the declaration or marking issued, and the technical documentation with its retention duty.

model.name: Offer / Quote
model.purpose: Represent one governed, versioned pre-contract commercial proposal so agents can understand who proposes what, to whom, for which price and terms, during which validity, with what evidence and response state, without confusing the proposal with a product master, negotiation, order, contract or legal formation decision.
model.scope_statement: Owns proposal identity, version, declared offer, quotation, estimate or informational profile; issuer and addressed-recipient roles; external product, service, right and resource references; lines, lots, bundles, options, alternatives and dependencies; quantities, units and eligibility; prices, currencies, formulas, tiers, recurring and usage terms; taxes, allowances, charges and totals; delivery, payment, quality, warranty, return, service-level, assumption, exclusion, rights and confidentiality terms; issue, effective, receipt, validity, response, expiry and knowledge times; attributable withdrawal, revocation, rejection, counter-offer and acceptance references; amendments, source, approval, quality, access, retention and loss-aware projections. Party, subject, catalogue, RFQ, negotiation, tender, contract, order, invoice, payment, fulfilment, response-event and legal-determination masters remain authoritative.
in_scope: Proposal identity, versions, profiles, parties by reference, offered subjects, lines, lots, bundles, quantities, eligibility, pricing, taxes, totals and commercial terms
Fulfilment conditions, validity, lifecycle, response references, amendments, evidence, provenance, validation, access, retention and interoperable projections
out_of_scope: Owning Party, Product, Service, Right, Catalogue, Price List, RFQ, Negotiation, Tender, Contract, Order, Invoice, Payment, Shipment, Performance, Response Event, Legal Decision or Records masters
Treating a quotation, estimate, acknowledgement, click, conduct or technical status as universal proof of legal offer, acceptance, formation or enforceability
Autonomous pricing approval, tax or legal determination, acceptance, signature, dispatch, publication, access widening or physical records disposition

boundary_notes.distinction: The unfrozen object parent may supply generic object context but grants no ownership, mutation or cascade authority.

boundary_notes.neighbor: RFQ, negotiation, tender, order and contract
boundary_notes.distinction: A request asks for a proposal, negotiation exchanges positions, a tender follows procurement rules, an order requests performance and a contract records obligations. The proposal references but does not absorb them.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Party, product, service, catalogue and price list
boundary_notes.distinction: These masters supply identities and source terms; the proposal owns only version-specific commercial assertions and references.
The proposal records attributable evidence and observed state but does not decide whether acceptance was effective or a contract formed under governing law.

boundary_notes.neighbor: UBL, schema.org, GS1, ODRL, PROV, JSON Schema and OpenAPI
boundary_notes.distinction: Each representation has different semantics and coverage; mappings are version-pinned and loss-declaring.

functions.name: Register an offer or quotation
functions.description: Governed operation to register an offer or quotation without autonomous pricing approval, tax determination, contract formation, acceptance, signature, dispatch, publication, access widening or records disposition.
preconditions: namespace, identity, issuer authority and profile checks pass
effects: a draft proposal exists without legal-effect inference

functions.name: Classify profile and jurisdiction
functions.description: Governed operation to classify profile and jurisdiction without autonomous pricing approval, tax determination, contract formation, acceptance, signature, dispatch, publication, access widening or records disposition.
outputs: qualified offer, quotation, estimate or informational classification
preconditions: classification criteria, jurisdiction, governing rules and uncertainty are explicit
effects: classification remains revisable and does not determine enforceability

functions.name: Compose subject lines and dependencies
functions.description: Governed operation to compose subject lines and dependencies without autonomous pricing approval, tax determination, contract formation, acceptance, signature, dispatch, publication, access widening or records disposition.
inputs: external product, service or right references
outputs: versioned lines, lots, bundles, options and dependencies
preconditions: subject masters resolve and cardinality, unit, option and dependency checks pass
effects: external subject lifecycles remain authoritative

functions.name: Calculate and bind pricing
functions.description: Governed operation to calculate and bind pricing without autonomous pricing approval, tax determination, contract formation, acceptance, signature, dispatch, publication, access widening or records disposition.
inputs: currency, quantity, tax, allowance and charge rules
preconditions: formula versions, units, currencies, rounding, tax jurisdiction and approval policy pass
effects: calculation produces evidence and never silently approves or mutates an issued price

functions.name: Bind commercial and fulfilment terms
functions.description: Governed operation to bind commercial and fulfilment terms without autonomous pricing approval, tax determination, contract formation, acceptance, signature, dispatch, publication, access widening or records disposition.
inputs: delivery, payment, warranty, service-level and rights terms
preconditions: term sources, dependencies, responsibility, jurisdiction and exceptions are explicit
effects: contract, order and fulfilment remain external

functions.name: Review, approve and issue a version
functions.description: Governed operation to review, approve and issue a version without autonomous pricing approval, tax determination, contract formation, acceptance, signature, dispatch, publication, access widening or records disposition.
outputs: immutable issued version and communication instructions
preconditions: pricing, tax, legal, commercial, access and approval checks pass
effects: the model records but does not autonomously sign, dispatch or publish

functions.name: Record communication and response events
functions.description: Governed operation to record communication and response events without autonomous pricing approval, tax determination, contract formation, acceptance, signature, dispatch, publication, access widening or records disposition.
inputs: attributable sent, received, withdrawal, revocation, rejection, counter-offer or acceptance evidence
outputs: immutable event references and observed lifecycle assertions
preconditions: actor, authority, channel, receipt semantics, time, source and uncertainty are explicit
effects: no event or status automatically determines contract formation

functions.name: Validate an offer or quotation
functions.description: Governed operation to validate an offer or quotation without autonomous pricing approval, tax determination, contract formation, acceptance, signature, dispatch, publication, access widening or records disposition.
preconditions: identity, totals, taxes, dates, eligibility, authority, lifecycle and projection checks execute
effects: errors are reported without autonomous legal or commercial action

functions.name: Amend, correct or supersede
functions.description: Governed operation to amend, correct or supersede without autonomous pricing approval, tax determination, contract formation, acceptance, signature, dispatch, publication, access widening or records disposition.
outputs: successor version, comparison and communication requirements
preconditions: reason, affected lines and terms, prior responses, validity, authority and retention checks pass
effects: prior issued versions remain resolvable

functions.name: Query, project, retain and audit
functions.description: Governed operation to query, project, retain and audit without autonomous pricing approval, tax determination, contract formation, acceptance, signature, dispatch, publication, access widening or records disposition.
outputs: filtered view, loss-declaring projection, retention result or audit event
preconditions: purpose, authority, privacy, mapping, digest, lifecycle and legal-hold checks pass
effects: representations never replace the canonical proposal and disposition stays external

composition.purpose: Resolve generic object context without granting ownership, mutation or cascade authority.

composition.target: Party, Product, Service, Right, Catalogue, Price List, RFQ, Negotiation, Tender, Contract, Order, Invoice, Payment, Fulfilment, Event and Records models
composition.purpose: Resolve authoritative external identities, processes, events and evidence without duplicating their lifecycles.

composition.target: CISG, UNIDROIT Principles, EU Consumer Rights, UBL 2.3, schema.org, GS1 Web Vocabulary, UN Recommendation 20, ISO 4217, ODRL 2.2, PROV-O, DQV, RFC 3339, JSON Schema 2020-12 and OpenAPI 3.1.1
composition.purpose: Project version-pinned legal, commerce, discovery, policy, provenance, quality, time, validation and API views with declared information loss.

owner_package_requirements: Dimension owner, namespace authority, accountable commercial owner and delegated pricing and legal authorities
Authoritative Party, Product, Service, Catalogue, Price List, RFQ, Negotiation, Tender, Contract, Order, Invoice, Payment, Fulfilment, Event and Records registries
Approved jurisdiction, tax, currency, unit, pricing, eligibility, delivery, payment, rights, privacy, retention and interoperability profiles
Role, delegation, segregation-of-duties, review, approval, issue, communication, response, amendment and agent-operation policies
dimension.namespace_guidance: Mint proposal, version, line, lot, price-component, term, event-reference, validation and projection IDs; preserve all external master identifiers.
registry_links: https://ver.cy/models/
https://ver.cy/model-agent-protocol.md

canonicalization_rules: Canonicalize by authoritative proposal identifier, issuer namespace and version head, never by title, recipient, issue date, total, filename or digest alone.
Keep offer or quote, party, product, service, catalogue, RFQ, negotiation, tender, contract, order, invoice, payment, fulfilment, response event and records independently identifiable.
patch_rules: Extensions declare profile, jurisdiction, identity, party, subject, line, quantity, price, tax, term, lifecycle, access and interoperability effects.
Issued versions are immutable; changes create linked successors with reason, affected terms, response impact, compatibility, migration and approval.
Never silently change profile, issuer, recipient, subject, quantity, price, currency, tax, total, term, validity, authority, response or legal-effect qualifier.
compatibility_rules: Ignore additive fields only when identity, version, profile, parties, subject, price, currency, taxes, terms, validity, authority, access and provenance survive.
Every projection pins specification or vocabulary version and declares loss in line, pricing, tax, term, response, lifecycle and authority semantics.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier for proposal, version, line, price component, term, event reference or artifact, qualified by issuer namespace and record kind.
Governed globally resolvable proposal or artifact IRI.
Dimension UUID or ULID when neither preceding identifier exists.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Use RFC 3339 timestamps with seconds and explicit offset or Z; distinguish issue, effective, receipt, validity, response, withdrawal, revocation, rejection, acceptance, expiry, observation, ingestion and knowledge times whenever they differ.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Store digest, media type, record kind, proposal and version IDs, profile, issuer, actor, distinct event and knowledge times, confidentiality marking and provenance.

policies: The proposal owns its commercial assertions and versions but not external parties, subjects, negotiations, requests, tenders, contracts, orders, invoices, payments, fulfilment, response events or legal determinations.
Offer, quotation, estimate and informational proposal are explicit profiles; labels and statuses alone never establish legal effect.
Issue, delivery, receipt, effectiveness, validity, response, expiry and formation determinations are separate assertions.
Agents cannot autonomously approve pricing, determine tax or legal effect, accept, sign, dispatch, publish, widen access or dispose records without delegated authority.

read: Resolve proposal head, versions, profile, parties, subjects, lines, pricing, taxes, totals, terms, validity, events, evidence, access and projection loss under the permitted view.
create: Bind identity, issuer, declared profile, purpose, recipient scope, jurisdiction, currency, source authority and initial lifecycle before commercial assertions are accepted.
update: Append successor lines, prices, taxes, terms, approvals, communications, responses, corrections and lifecycle assertions with reason, authority, expected revision, event time and knowledge time.
delete: Apply legal hold, commercial-record, consumer, tax, privacy and adopting-Dimension retention policy; withdraw or tombstone only the catalogue view without cascading to external masters, and let authoritative systems execute physical disposition.

roles.name: Proposal owner
responsibilities: Own purpose, scope, profile, lifecycle, compatibility and accountable use.

roles.name: Commercial and pricing owner
responsibilities: Own subjects, quantities, price inputs, formulas, discounts, charges, totals and approval evidence.

roles.name: Tax and legal authority
responsibilities: Own jurisdictional tax treatment, legal profile, required disclosures, formation interpretation and limitations.

roles.name: Sales or procurement operator
responsibilities: Own party, RFQ, communication, delivery, receipt, response and amendment coordination.

roles.name: Reviewer and approving authority
responsibilities: Own validation, exceptions, segregation of duties and authorization to issue.

roles.name: Access and records authority
responsibilities: Own confidentiality, privacy, disclosure, retention, legal hold and disposition policy.

roles.name: Interoperability steward
responsibilities: Own UBL, schema.org, GS1, ODRL, PROV, JSON, API mappings, conformance evidence and declared loss.

access.default_rule: Deny draft, non-public, negotiated, personal, confidential, commercially sensitive, cost, margin, discount, tax, approval, recipient-specific or response data unless a purpose-bound policy permits the minimum necessary view.
exceptions: Declared commercial, legal, tax, audit, dispute, regulatory or subject-rights access must cite authority, scope, purpose and time limit and must be logged.
audit_requirements: Log actor, agent, role, purpose, proposal and version, operation, authority, policy, RFC 3339 time, affected lines or terms, source revision and outcome without duplicating restricted commercial data.

read_order: Read Dimension namespace, commercial, pricing, tax, legal, privacy, retention and agent policies.
Read this proposal and linked party, subject, catalogue, RFQ, negotiation, contract, order, invoice, payment, fulfilment, event and records models before mutation.

Jurisdiction and sector profiles, legal-effect determinations and independent external review remain deferred.

known_omissions: Claude and Grok each timed out on one bounded attempt; no independent external result was admitted.
The WM-OBJ-003 parent signal has no frozen approved relation and grants no cascade authority.
Public procurement, securities, insurance, healthcare, utilities, travel, telecom, software subscription, construction and other sector profiles need separate rules.
National contract, tax, consumer, electronic-signature, records and privacy rules require jurisdiction profiles and authorized legal review.
Schema.org is a discovery vocabulary and does not establish legal effect or full transactional conformance.
conflicts: Offer, quote, estimate, proposal, invitation, RFQ, tender, counter-offer, order and contract are related but not interchangeable.
Issue, sending, delivery, receipt, effectiveness, availability, validity, acceptance and contract formation are distinct assertions.
List, unit, net, estimated, ranged, recurring, usage, tax, charge, subtotal and payable amounts must not be collapsed.
Silence, acknowledgement, click, conduct or technical status does not universally prove acceptance or enforceability.

boundaryDecision.rationale: The root is a versioned pre-contract commercial proposal aggregate with explicit legal-offer, quotation, estimate and informational profiles. Parties, products, services, catalogues, RFQs, negotiations, tenders, contracts, orders, invoices, payments, fulfilment, response events, legal determinations and records remain external masters.

decisions.concept: Offer, quotation, estimate and informational proposal
decisions.rationale: The shared structure is useful, but declared intent, definiteness, governing rules and legal effect differ; no label alone determines an operative legal offer.
The registry parent signal has no frozen canonical relation and grants no ownership, mutation or cascade authority.
Party, subject, catalogue, price list, RFQ, negotiation, tender, contract, order, invoice, payment and fulfilment identities and lifecycles remain external.

decisions.concept: Line, lot, bundle, option and dependency semantics
decisions.rationale: Composition preserves stable line and term identities plus alternative, substitution, minimum, partial and all-or-none rules rather than flattening them into text.

List, unit, base, net, fixed, estimated, ranged, tiered, recurring, usage, tax, allowance, charge, subtotal and payable values stay distinct with currency, unit, quantity basis, formula, validity and provenance.

Sending, delivery, receipt, acknowledgement, withdrawal, revocation, rejection, counter-offer, acceptance evidence and formation determinations are separately attributable; no status automatically proves legal effect.

Issue, effective, receipt, validity, response, delivery, withdrawal, revocation, rejection, acceptance, expiry, observation, ingestion and knowledge times remain distinct and RFC 3339 timestamps require seconds and offset.
CISG, UNIDROIT Principles and EU consumer requirements provide scoped reference profiles; national contract, tax, signature, privacy and records rules remain jurisdiction-qualified.
UBL, schema.org, GS1, ODRL, PROV, DQV, JSON Schema and OpenAPI expose different subsets and never replace canonical proposal semantics.

One bounded Claude Sonnet and one bounded Grok attempt each timed out after 120 seconds. Codex separately audits the frozen validated result and comparison locally without tools or new research facts; assurance remains reviewable-draft.

publicationHolds: Absence-of-external-review hold: one Claude Sonnet and one Grok attempt for WM-ECO-021 each timed out after 120 seconds; no external research result was admitted.
Relation hold: WM-OBJ-003 is only a parent signal and no model relation is canonically approved for this aggregate.

Boundary hold: offer or quote, party, product, service, catalogue, price list, RFQ, negotiation, tender, contract, order, invoice, payment, fulfilment, response event, legal determination and records must retain separate identities.

Legal-effect hold: offer, quotation, estimate and informational profiles require explicit intent, governing rules and jurisdiction; no label, click, acknowledgement, conduct or status universally proves acceptance, formation or enforceability.

Pricing hold: every amount requires type, currency, unit or quantity basis, inclusion and exclusion, tax and charge treatment, formula or source, validity, rounding, approval and uncertainty qualifiers.

Temporal hold: issue, effective, receipt, validity, response, delivery, withdrawal, revocation, rejection, acceptance, expiry, observation, ingestion and knowledge time must never be silently collapsed; timestamps require seconds and timezone offset.
Authority hold: pricing approval, tax determination, legal classification, acceptance, signature, dispatch, publication, access widening and disposition require delegated accountable authority.
Jurisdiction hold: CISG, UNIDROIT Principles and EU consumer requirements are scoped profiles; national contract, tax, signature, privacy, records and sector rules require separate validation.
Interoperability hold: every UBL, schema.org, GS1, UNECE, ISO 4217, ODRL, PROV, DQV, JSON Schema and OpenAPI projection requires version pins, conformance evidence and information-loss declarations.

Privacy hold: recipient-specific prices, discounts, cost, margin, tax, negotiation, approval, contact, response and commercially sensitive data require purpose-bound access, minimization and retention controls.
Independent external review was explicitly waived by the repository owner; this codex-only result remains a reviewable draft.

Create public procurement, securities, insurance, healthcare, utilities, travel, telecom, software subscription, construction and jurisdiction-specific profiles.
Conformance-test lines, dependencies, quantities, units, prices, taxes, totals, validity, amendments and projections against concrete UBL and commerce examples.
Validate organization-specific pricing, discount, tax, approval, signing, dispatch, publication, access, retention and disposition policies.
Obtain authorized legal and tax review before making jurisdiction-specific formation, enforceability, disclosure or tax claims.
Obtain independent external research review before promoting beyond reviewable-draft assurance.
